anf_compare.notes: Translated from the PG 74 Greek; no published English version was used for wording.

bible_refs.note: ἵνα διαγγελῇ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐν πάσῃ τῇ γῇ, given in the third person as in u08-rem-close; ἔνδειξιν τῆς… ἰσχύος picks up ἐνδείξωμαι… τὴν δύναμίν μου.
Quoted without εἰ δέ and without αὐτοῦ after τὸ δυνατόν; 'his' supplied by English idiom for the article.
Cyril paraphrases: ἵνα ὠφελήσῃ σκεύη ἐλέους for Paul's ἵνα γνωρίσῃ τὸν πλοῦτον τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ σκεύη ἐλέους.
οὐ μόνον ἐξ Ἰουδαίων, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐξ ἐθνῶν, in the first person plural (κεκλήμεθα).
Lemma: Ὡς καὶ ἐν τῷ Ὡσηὲ λέγει.
LXX Hosea 2:25 (English 2:23), quoted by Paul in Romans 9:25: τὸν οὐ λαόν μου λαόν μου; Cyril's οὐκ ἦμεν αὐτοῦ λαός… ἀλλ' ἠλεήθημεν applies it. 1 Peter 2:10 uses the same pair.
Lemma and τὸ κατάλειμμα σωθήσεται (Byzantine κατάλειμμα; critical text ὑπόλειμμα).
Source of Romans 9:27–28 (LXX: ὡς ἡ ἄμμος τῆς θαλάσσης, τὸ κατάλειμμα αὐτῶν σωθήσεται· λόγον συντελῶν καὶ συντέμνων).
Lemma λόγον γὰρ συντελῶν καὶ συντέμνων, repeated in the comment.
Lemma Ἰσραὴλ δὲ διώκων νόμον δικαιοσύνης; 'missed its hope' paraphrases εἰς νόμον δικαιοσύνης οὐκ ἔφθασε.
Close paraphrase: τὰ ἔθνη τὰ μὴ διώκοντα δικαιοσύνην κατέλαβε δικαιοσύνην.
Paul's reason (ὅτι οὐκ ἐκ πίστεως ἀλλ' ὡς ἐξ ἔργων) restated as refusal of salvation through faith.
Lemma λίθον προσκόμματος (9:33; 9:32 has τῷ λίθῳ τοῦ προσκόμματος).
LXX λίθου προσκόμματι; the stumbling element of Paul's combined citation, which Cyril paraphrases as ὄλισθος and περιπίπτειν.
LXX ἐμβαλῶ εἰς τὰ θεμέλια Σιὼν λίθον… ἔντιμον; Cyril's εἰς τὰ θεμέλια Σιών and λίθος τίμιος. Cited at both clauses.
Lemma Μαρτυρῶ γὰρ αὐτοῖς; 'zeal for God' from ὅτι ζῆλον Θεοῦ ἔχουσιν.

choices.english: the strength that is in him
choices.why: τῆς ἐνούσης ἰσχύος αὐτῷ: 'the strength that is in him', i.e. in God, the subject of προσεχρήσατο.

choices.term: Ἔσωσε δέ φησιν λόγον συντελῶν καὶ συντέμνων
choices.english: He saved, he says, by “completing and cutting short the word”
choices.why: Ἔσωσε δέ φησιν λόγον συντελῶν καὶ συντέμνων: Cyril's gloss on the lemma, with ἔσωσε ('he saved') and no object; rendered 'He saved, he says, by “completing and cutting short the word”'. Nothing supplied as object.
λόγιον… συντετμημένον: 'cut-short saying' (λόγιον can mean an oracle); kept close to the lemma's συντέμνων.
Ὢ παραδόξου πράγματος: Cyril's own exclamation, put as Paul's sense ('and says'); not marked as quotation because it is not Paul's wording.

choices.english: the boasts they had, as in shadows
choices.why: τὰ ὡς ἐν σκιαῖς αὐχήματα: 'the boasts they had, as in shadows', i.e. privileges of the law, which Cyril calls a shadow.
ἀμείνους γένοιντο τοῦ κακοῦ: 'might rise above the evil' (lit. 'become better than the evil').

pass_a_gloss: [completes τουτέστιν εἰς from u09-open] such (touto) of baseness (phaulotetos) he drove through (dielase) ways (tropon), as to be henceforth (loipon) vessel of wrath and of destruction (apoleias). This one God made use of (prosechresato) toward showing (endeixin) of the strength (ischyos) in him, that his name may be proclaimed (diangele) in all the earth, and that he having suffered (pathon) might be seen worthy (axios) of suffering; to whom indeed suffering was owed (opheileto) for first sins (protas hamartias) even if he had not offended (proskekrouke) through the second. Therefore let be dissolved (lelystho) every blame (momos) and nonsense (phlyaria) against God; for wishing to show the wrath (orgen) and to make known the powerful (to dynaton) he bore (enenken) in much long suffering (makrothymia) vessels of wrath fitted (katertismena) for destruction, that he might benefit (ophelese) vessels of mercy (eleous), that is, the ones having been shown mercy (eleemenous) through faith (pisteos); for we have been called (keklemetha) not only from Jews, but also from nations (ethnon). [lemma Romans 9:25] As also in Hosea he says. But also the servants (therapeutai) of idols (eidolon), not knowing the by nature (physei) and truly (alethos) God, we were not his people (laos); but we were shown mercy (eleethemen) through faith, and we have come under him, and we have been called through grace (charitos), and we have been justified (dedikaiometha) and sanctified (hegiasmetha) through Christ. [lemma Romans 9:27] If be the number of the sons of Israel as the sand (ammos) of the sea. Therefore even if Israel be many as the sand (psammos), the remnant (kataleimma) will be saved (sothesetai); that is, the ones having been justified through the faith in Christ; and this has come about, God having had mercy on (kateleesantos) them. [lemma Romans 9:28] For a word completing (synteleon) and cutting short (syntemnon). He saved (esose), he says, a word completing and cutting short, that is, displaying (apophenas) to us the gospel preaching (euangelikon kerygma) a well formed (euphyes) and concise (syntomon) and, that I may speak thus, cut short (syntetmemenon) oracle (logion). For the law (nomos) and the prophets through much circuit (kyklou) of words scarcely present (paristosi) to us through the letter (grammatos) the notions (ennoias) of the things said; but the gospel preaching is simple (haploun) and a word cut short (logos syntetmemenos). [lemma Romans 9:31] But Israel pursuing (dioken) a law of righteousness (dikaiosynes). Rendering (apodidous) therefore the causes (aitias) of not all Jews having been saved, at once he weaves into (epiplekei) the argument wonder (thauma), and says: O paradoxical (paradoxou) thing; the multitude (plethys) of the ones straying (planomenon), not having aim (skopon) at all to do good (agathoergesai), has been justified (dedikaiotai), but Israel, although being tutored (paidagogoumenos) toward righteousness by the law through Moses, missed (diemarte) the hope (elpidos) and became without share (ametochos) of the gift (doreas) toward this. What then the cause, clear: for they did not accept (prosekanto) the salvation (soterian) through faith and the justification (dikaiosin) in Christ, but they thought to suffice them the boasts (auchemata) as in shadows (skiais). [lemma Romans 9:33] A stone (lithon) of stumbling (proskommatos). For surely we do not say that for this was set (etethe) Christ in Israel, but since this had been foreknown (proegnosto) by God, he forevoiced (proanapephoneke) necessarily (anankaios) the to be, that will lie (keisetai) a slipping (olisthos) into the foundations (themelia) of Zion, and some of the unintelligent (asyneton) are about to fall upon (peripiptein) it, and to suffer this from disobedience (apeitheias). And he made the foretelling (proagoreusin) usefully (chresimos), not that they might stumble (proskopseian), but that having foreknown (proegnokotes) they might become better (ameinous) than the evil. Therefore Christ has been set as a precious stone (lithos timios), but for the ones stumbling from unbelief (apistias), ruin (olethros) was the loss (zemia); but for the ones having believed, life (zoe) and justification (dikaiosis) the gain (kerdos). [lemma Romans 10:2] For I bear witness (martyro) to them. He bears witness therefore to them the zeal (zelon) toward God; but he convicts (elenchei) them having strayed (peplanemenous); because it being needful (deon) to marvel at (thaumazein) Christ from the things he was doing as by nature (physei) [continues 'God' in u09-rem mid].
pass_b_english: …he drove so far into wicked ways as to be from then on a vessel of wrath and of destruction. God made use of this man to display the strength that is in himself, so that his name might be proclaimed in all the earth (Romans 9:17), and so that Pharaoh, when he suffered, might be seen to deserve his suffering; for suffering was owed to him for his first sins, even if he had not offended by his later ones. So let every reproach and every idle charge against God be dismissed. For “desiring to show his wrath and to make known his power, he endured with much patience vessels of wrath prepared for destruction” (Romans 9:22), in order to benefit vessels of mercy (Romans 9:23), that is, those who have received mercy through faith; for we have been called not only from the Jews but also from the Gentiles (Romans 9:24).

“As indeed he says in Hosea” (Romans 9:25). We too, the servants of idols, who did not know the one who is God by nature and in truth, were not his people (Hosea 2:23); but we have received mercy through faith, have come under him, have been called through grace, and have been justified and sanctified through Christ.

“Though the number of the sons of Israel be as the sand of the sea” (Romans 9:27). So even if Israel were as many as the sand, “the remnant will be saved” (Romans 9:27; Isaiah 10:22), that is, those who have been justified through faith in Christ; and this has come about because God had mercy on them. “For he is completing and cutting short the word” (Romans 9:28). He saved, he says, by “completing and cutting short the word”; that is, he declared to us the preaching of the gospel as an apt and concise and, so to speak, cut-short saying. For the law and the prophets, by a long circuit of words, scarcely set before us through the letter the meaning of what they say; but the preaching of the gospel is simple and a word cut short.

“But Israel, pursuing a law of righteousness” (Romans 9:31). In giving the reasons why not all the Jews have been saved, he at once weaves wonder into his argument and says: What a strange thing! The crowd of those who had gone astray, with no aim at all of doing good, has been justified (Romans 9:30), while Israel, though trained toward righteousness by the law given through Moses, missed its hope and has had no share in the gift that leads to it (Romans 9:31). What the cause is, then, is plain: they did not accept salvation through faith and justification in Christ, but thought that the boasts they had, as in shadows, were enough for them (Romans 9:32).

“A stone of stumbling” (Romans 9:33). Surely we do not say that Christ was set in Israel for this purpose; but since this was foreknown to God, he of necessity foretold what was to be: that a cause of slipping would lie in the foundations of Zion, and that some of the foolish would fall upon it and suffer this from their disobedience (Isaiah 8:14; Isaiah 28:16). He made the prediction for their benefit, not that they should stumble, but that, knowing it beforehand, they might rise above the evil. So Christ has been laid as a precious stone (Isaiah 28:16); but for those who stumble out of unbelief the loss was ruin, while for those who have believed the gain is life and justification.

“For I bear them witness” (Romans 10:2). He bears them witness, then, to their zeal for God; yet he convicts them of having gone astray, because, when they ought to have marvelled at Christ, from the works he was doing, as being by nature…

τοῦτο φαυλότητος διήλασε τρόπων, ὡς σκεῦος εἶναι λοιπὸν ὀργῆς τε καὶ ἀπωλείας.
τούτῳ Θεὸς προσεχρήσατο πρὸς ἔνδειξιν τῆς ἐνούσης ἰσχύος αὐτῷ, ἵνα διαγγελῇ τὸ
ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐν πάσῃ τῇ γῇ, καὶ ἵνα παθὼν αὐτὸς ὁρῷτο τοῦ 233 παθεῖν ἄξιος· ᾧ γε τὸ
παθεῖν ὠφείλετο διὰ πρώτας ἁμαρτίας καὶ εἰ μὴ προσκέκρουκε διὰ τῶν δευτέρων.
οὐκοῦν λελύσθω πᾶς μῶμος καὶ φλυαρία κατὰ Θεοῦ· θέλων γὰρ ἐνδείξασθαι τὴν ὀργὴν
καὶ γνωρίσαι τὸ δυνατὸν ἤνεγκεν ἐν πολλῇ μακροθυμίᾳ σκεύη ὀργῆς κατηρτισμένα εἰς
ἀπώλειαν, ἵνα ὠφελήσῃ σκεύη ἐλέους, τουτέστι τοὺς ἠλεημένους διὰ πίστεως·
κεκλήμεθα γὰρ οὐ μόνον ἐξ Ἰουδαίων, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐξ ἐθνῶν. Ὡς καὶ ἐν τῷ Ὠσηὲ λέγει.
Ἀλλὰ καὶ οἱ τῶν εἰδώλων θεραπευταὶ, οὐκ εἰδότες τὸν φύσει καὶ ἀληθῶς Θεὸν, οὐκ
ἦμεν αὐτοῦ λαός· ἀλλ' ἠλεήθημεν διὰ πίστεως, καὶ ὑπ' αὐτὸν γεγόναμεν, καὶ κεκλήμεθα
διὰ χάριτος, δεδικαιώμεθά τε καὶ ἡγιάσμεθα διὰ Χριστοῦ. Ἐὰν ᾖ ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν υἱῶν

25

Ἰσραὴλ ὡς ἡ ἄμμος τῆς θαλάσσης. Οὐκοῦν κἂν πολλοὶ εἶεν ὡς ἡ ψάμμος ὁ Ἰσραὴλ, τὸ
κατάλειμμα σωθήσεται· τουτέστιν, οἱ διὰ πίστεως τῆς εἰς Χριστὸν δεδικαιωμένοι· τοῦτο
δὲ γέγονεν, αὐτοὺς τοῦ Θεοῦ κατηλεήσαντος. Λόγον γὰρ συντελῶν καὶ συντέμνων.
Ἔσωσε δέ φησιν λόγον συντελῶν καὶ συντέμνων, τουτέστιν εὐφυὲς καὶ σύντομον καὶ
ἵν' οὕτως εἴπω συντετμημένον λόγιον ἡμῖν ἀποφήνας τὸ εὐαγγελικὸν κήρυγμα. ὁ γὰρ
νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται διὰ πολλοῦ κύκλου λόγων μόλις ἡμῖν τὰς τῶν λεγομένων
ἐννοίας διὰ τοῦ γράμματος παριστῶσι· τὸ 234 δὲ κήρυγμα τὸ εὐαγγελικὸν ἁπλοῦν τέ
ἐστι καὶ λόγος συντετμημένος. Ἰσραὴλ δὲ διώκων νόμον δικαιοσύνης.
Ἀποδιδοὺς τοίνυν τὰς αἰτίας τοῦ μὴ πάντας σεσῶσθαι Ἰουδαίους, εὐθὺς
ἐπιπλέκει τῷ λόγῳ θαῦμα, καί φησιν Ὢ παραδόξου πράγματος· ἡ τῶν πλανωμένων
πληθὺς μὴ ἔχουσα σκοπὸν ὅλως ἀγαθοεργῆσαι, δεδικαίωται, ὁ δὲ Ἰσραὴλ, καίτοι τῷ διὰ
Μωσέως νόμῳ πρὸς δικαιοσύνην παιδαγωγούμενος, διήμαρτε τῆς ἐλπίδος καὶ ἀμέτοχος
γέγονε τῆς εἰς τοῦτο δωρεᾶς. τίς οὖν ἡ αἰτία, σαφής· οὐ γὰρ προσήκαντο τὴν διὰ
πίστεως σωτηρίαν καὶ τὴν ἐν Χριστῷ δικαίωσιν, ἐνόμισαν δὲ αὐτοῖς ἀρκεῖν τὰ ὡς ἐν
σκιαῖς αὐχήματα. Λίθον προσκόμματος. Οὐ γὰρ δήπου φαμὲν ὅτι διὰ τοῦτο ἐτέθη
Χριστὸς ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ, ἀλλ' ἐπειδὴ τοῦτο προέγνωστο τῷ Θεῷ, τὸ ἐσόμενον
προαναπεφώνηκεν ἀναγκαίως, ὡς κείσεται μὲν ὄλισθος εἰς τὰ θεμέλια Σιὼν, μέλλουσι
δὲ περιπίπτειν αὐτῷ τῶν ἀσυνέτων τινὲς, καὶ τοῦτο πάσχειν ἐξ ἀπειθείας. ἐποίειτο δὲ
τὴν προαγόρευσιν χρησίμως, οὐχ ἵνα προσκόψειαν, ἀλλ' ἵνα προεγνωκότες ἀμείνους
γένοιντο τοῦ κακοῦ. οὐκοῦν τέθειται μὲν ὁ Χριστὸς ὡς λίθος τίμιος, πλὴν τοῖς μὲν ἐξ
ἀπιστίας προσκόπτουσιν, ὄλεθρος ἦν ἡ ζημία· τοῖς δὲ πεπιστευκόσι, ζωὴ καὶ δικαίωσις
τὸ κέρδος. Μαρτυρῶ γὰρ αὐτοῖς. Μαρτυρεῖ τοίνυν αὐτοῖς τὸν εἰς Θεὸν ζῆλον· πλὴν
ἐλέγχει πεπλανημένους· ὅτι δέον θαυμάζειν τὸν Χριστὸν ἐξ ὧν 235 ἐποίει ὡς φύσει
reviewer: claude (Wave A review, clause by clause against the Greek)
review_notes: Fixed in place in tr8.json. 'God made use of him to display the strength that is in him' left it unclear whose strength (Pharaoh's or God's). τῆς ἐνούσης ἰσχύος αὐτῷ refers to God, the subject, so now 'God made use of this man (τούτῳ) to display the strength that is in himself'. Rest checked clause by clause against the source: faithful, citations right (Hosea 2:23 = LXX 2:25), no debris.
Copy-text: PG 74; Fragmenta in Romanos via Khazarzar (Fragmenta in sancti Pauli epistulam ad Romanos.pdf).
Section opens mid-sentence, completing τουτέστιν εἰς from the close of u09-open; rendered with a leading ellipsis.
τῆς ἐνούσης ἰσχύος αὐτῷ: 'the strength that is in him', i.e. in God, the subject of προσεχρήσατο.

διὰ πρώτας ἁμαρτίας… διὰ τῶν δευτέρων: Pharaoh's earlier sins (idolatry, oppression of Israel, named in u09-open) already deserved punishment, apart from his later resistance; rendered 'first sins… later ones'.
μῶμος καὶ φλυαρία: 'reproach and idle charge'.

Ἔσωσε δέ φησιν λόγον συντελῶν καὶ συντέμνων: Cyril's gloss on the lemma, with ἔσωσε ('he saved') and no object; rendered 'He saved, he says, by “completing and cutting short the word”'. Nothing supplied as object.
λόγιον… συντετμημένον: 'cut-short saying' (λόγιον can mean an oracle); kept close to the lemma's συντέμνων.
Ὢ παραδόξου πράγματος: Cyril's own exclamation, put as Paul's sense ('and says'); not marked as quotation because it is not Paul's wording.
τὰ ὡς ἐν σκιαῖς αὐχήματα: 'the boasts they had, as in shadows', i.e. privileges of the law, which Cyril calls a shadow.
ἀμείνους γένοιντο τοῦ κακοῦ: 'might rise above the evil' (lit. 'become better than the evil').
οὐκ ἦμεν… ἀλλ' ἠλεήθημεν… δεδικαιώμεθά τε καὶ ἡγιάσμεθα may also echo 1 Corinthians 6:11 (ἡγιάσθητε, ἐδικαιώθητε); possible allusion only, so not cited inline.
Page numbers 233, 234 and 235 and the footer numeral '25' are edition apparatus and are omitted.
Section ends mid-sentence at ὡς φύσει; the next row opens with Θεόν. The English keeps the cut at 'as being by nature…'; u09-rem-mid resumes with '…God'.
